description: Synthetic contrast case where an older consumer rule permits an action after a newer applicable authority has already restricted that action.
applicable_permission_or_restriction_ter: Semantic assessment requests are excluded after the restrictive policy becomes effective unless an applicable exception or delegation is in force.
The restrictive authority supersedes the earlier consumer permission rule for the examined action from its effective time.

E-X1-RULE-001.statement: The consumer decision path used the legacy rule, under which submission of the semantic assessment request was permitted.

E-X1-SEM-001.statement: The synthetic provider-facing semantic assessment completed with an acceptable component result.

E-X1-AUTH-001.statement: From the effective time onward, submission of the semantic assessment request is excluded unless an applicable exception or delegation is in force.

E-X1-EXC-001.statement: The applicable authority record affirmatively confirms that no exception or delegation applies to the examined action at the decision time.

evidence_linkage.relationship: explains why the consumer decision path allowed the action to proceed
establishes the newer restrictive authority and its effective time
affirmatively establishes that no overriding exception or delegation applies
establishes an operative exclusion for the examined action at the decision time

notes: Synthetic offline fixture; no live Jev call is required or implied.
The applied consumer rule and the applicable permission authority are intentionally different.
The difference between applied_rule_reference and authority_reference is not itself an evidence conflict.
The NOT_SUPPORTED result relies on an operative newer restriction plus affirmative evidence that no overriding exception or delegation applies.
If exception or delegation applicability were unresolved, the permission result would instead be INDETERMINATE.
Post-response assessment does not imply that the earlier request was prevented.
